MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

PARTNER INFORMATION
Partner Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Pregnancy with family history of cystic fibrosis. Carrier screening requested for both partners.

TEST PERFORMED
Cystic Fibrosis Carrier Screening Panel
Methodology: Multiplex oligonucleotide ligation assay (MOLA) testing for 31 common CFTR gene mutations
Gene analyzed: CFTR (NM_000492.4)
Mutation coverage: Approximately 95% of cystic fibrosis mutations in the general population

RESULTS

1. FEMALE PARTNER ([redacted name]):
   Result: NEGATIVE
   No mutations detected among the 31 CFTR mutations tested
   
2. MALE PARTNER ([redacted name]):
   Result: NEGATIVE
   No mutations detected among the 31 CFTR mutations tested

MUTATIONS TESTED
The following 31 mutations were analyzed: F508del, G542X, G551D, W1282X, N1303K, R553X, 621+1G>T, R117H, 1717-1G>A, A455E, R560T, G85E, R334W, R347P, 711+1G>T, 1898+1G>A, 2184delA, 1078delT, 3849+10kbC>T, 2789+5G>A, 3120+1G>A, I507del, F508C, S549N, S549R, G551S, R1162X, G1244E, G1349D, D1152H, L206W

RISK ASSESSMENT

3. CARRIER RISK CALCULATIONS:
   a) Female partner:
      - Pre-test carrier risk (with positive family history): ~1/32
      - Post-test residual carrier risk: ~1/620
      
   b) Male partner:
      - Pre-test carrier risk (general population): ~1/25
      - Post-test residual carrier risk: ~1/400

4. REPRODUCTIVE RISK:
   Combined risk of having a child affected with cystic fibrosis: <1/990,000
   This represents a significant reduction from the pre-test risk.

INTERPRETATION
Both partners tested negative for the 31 most common CFTR mutations. While this significantly reduces the likelihood of being carriers, it does not eliminate the possibility entirely, as this panel covers approximately 95% of CF-causing mutations in the general population. The residual risk calculations take into account the detection rate of the test and the positive family history in the female partner.

The combined reproductive risk of less than 1 in 990,000 is substantially lower than the general population risk of 1 in 2,500 for having a child with cystic fibrosis.

RECOMMENDATIONS
5. Based on these results, prenatal testing for cystic fibrosis is not indicated.
6. No further CF carrier testing is recommended at this time.
7. Genetic counseling is available to discuss these results and any remaining concerns.
8. If additional family history information becomes available that suggests a specific rare CFTR mutation, expanded sequencing may be considered.

LIMITATIONS
This test detects only the mutations listed above and does not rule out the presence of other rare mutations in the CFTR gene. Full gene sequencing would be required to detect rare variants not included in this panel.

This test was developed and validated by [redacted name] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Laboratory Director
CAP: [redacted ID] CLIA: [redacted ID]
